Control Spike-In and Solids Separation Thaw a vial of Calf-Guard® Bovine Rota Coronavirus vaccine ( Zoetis Cat. No. 11712 ) on ice. Calf-Guard contains an attenuated bovine coronavirus (hereafter BCoV). To prepare a BCoV control spike-in, dissolve the vaccine in 1 mL of TE buffer (Fisher Scientific Cat. No. BP2473500). Divide the resuspended BCoV control spike-in into 10 separate 100 µL aliquots and store them at -20 °C. These are single-use aliquots. Dilute BCoV 1:10 in nuclease-free DEPC-treated water (Fisher Scientific Cat. No. AM9906). Add 40 µl of the 1:10 BCoV control spike-in to each conical tube. Load centrifuge tubes in the rotor. Centrifuge the samples at 5000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C with the brake set at 0. We used a Sorvall RC5B centrifuge with an SS34 rotor. Note: The paper that accompanies this protocol includes data that demonstrates the positive effect of pasteurization and of storing the samples in PEG/NaCl at 4 °C for at least 24 hours. The protocol includes a control for determining recovery efficiency. This is achieved by spiking the wastewater samples with a known amount of a bovine coronavirus. The protocol was initially developed using Phi6, but due to the rapid degradation of Phi6 in wastewater, we switched to bovine coronavirus.

Supernatant Filtration Without disturbing the pellet, carefully transfer 40 mL of each sample supernatant to a 150 mL Vacuum Filter/Storage Bottle System (Corning™ Cat. No. 430769) or load a 50 mL syringe (Becton Dickinson™ Cat. No. 309654) that has a 0.22 µm filter (MilliporeSigma™ Cat. No. SLGP033RB) attached to it. Attach a disposable vacuum filter system to the laboratory stationary vacuum line or to a manifold connected to an electric vacuum pump. Turn on the vacuum line and filter until all liquid has passed through the filter. If using a syringe filter, pass the wastewater through the filter manually. Transfer filtrate to a 50 mL polypropylene Oak Ridge tube (ThermoFisher™ Cat. No. 3139-0030). Note: Tubes and syringes can be reused if bleach-sterilized and autoclaved.

Centrifugation Remove tubes from the 4 °C refrigerator and add 100 µl of a 2% safranin solution (Sigma-Aldrich Cat. No. 1092170500) to the tubes. Invert the tubes several times to mix well. Prior to centrifugation, mark the tube where the pellet is expected to precipitate. This will help determine pellet location when examining later. Centrifuge the tubes at 12,000 x g for 120 minutes at 4 °C with the brake set at 0. If no safranin is added, the pellet may be invisible. With added safranin, the pellet appears pale pink. Remove the majority of supernatant by decanting. Pour supernatant carefully from the side of the tube opposite to the pellet. Collect the supernatant in a liquids container as biohazardous waste to be autoclaved. Centrifuge the tubes again at 12,000 x g for 5 minutes at 4 °C. Remove any remaining liquid with a sterile glass Pasteur pipette (Fisher Scientific™ Cat. No. 22-183632). Note: When using Pasteur pipettes, care must be taken to decontaminate the rubber bulbs by cleaning with 10% bleach and leaving overnight.

RNA Extraction TRIzol protocol Phase Separation Resuspend the pellet with 1.5 mL of TRIzol (Invitrogen™ Cat. No. 15596018) by shaking the tube vigorously for at least 45 seconds*. Let the tube rest at room temperature for 5 minutes. Split the 1.5 mL of TRIzol resuspension into 2 equivalent amounts and transfer to 1.5mL microcentrifuge tubes (USA Scientific 1615-5510). Add 150 μl of chloroform (Fisher Scientific™ Cat. No. BP1145-1) to TRIzol resuspension to each of the tubes. (chloroform:TRIzol = 1:5 ratio). Invert the tube several times to mix. Centrifuge the sample at 12,000 g for 15 minutes at 4 °C. Carefully remove the aqueous phase (top layer) from each tube and pool it into one tube. For best results, try not to aspirate any of the bottom layer. It is better to not recover the whole top layer than accidentally aspirate the bottom layer. * It is crucial for the success of the protocol to completely dissolve the pellet before extracting RNA. We have developed a visualization step using the staining agent safranin that is strongly recommended with this protocol. Note: Handle chloroform with care and use a fume hood/biological safety cabinet to avoid inhaling fumes. Consult the SDS before use. RNA Extraction Add 600 μl of isopropanol (Fisher Scientific™ Cat. No. BP26181) into the aqueous phase (isopropanol: aqueous phase = 1:1 ratio), and invert the tube several times to mix. Incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes. Centrifuge at 12,000 g for 10 minutes at 4 °C. A pink pellet can be seen at the bottom or on the side of the tube. Decant and discard the supernatant. RNA Wash and Elution Add 1 mL of 75% ethanol (Fisher Scientific™ Cat. No. A4094) (100% ethanol:nuclease-free water = 3:1) to wash the pellet. Centrifuge 12,000 g for 3 minutes at 4 °C. Discard supernatant. Repeat wash once again with 1 mL of freshly made 75 % ethanol. Discard supernatant, air dry for 5-10 minutes (do not over-dry the pellet). Resuspend the pellet in 30 µl of nuclease-free water , let it sit at room temperature for 5 minutes before any downstream steps.

steps.title: Sample Handling
steps.instruction: Maintain wastewater samples at 4°C at all times after collection and keep containers closed throughout the procedure unless otherwise specified.

steps.title: Pasteurization
steps.instruction: Pasteurize wastewater samples in their original containers (~240 ml) using a preheated 60°C water bath.

substeps.instruction: Place containers in the 60°C water bath.
Briefly open one sample to introduce a temperature probe and close immediately.
Pasteurize for 60 minutes once the internal temperature of the samples reaches 60°C (typically takes 30-60 minutes to reach this temperature).
Prepare a method blank by adding 40 mL of deionized water into a separate, labeled 50 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Sample Aliquoting
steps.instruction: Transfer pasteurized samples to conical tubes for further processing.

substeps.instruction: Remove containers from the water bath and wipe away any remaining liquid from the outside of each container.
Aliquot 40 mL of the pasteurized sample into 50 mL conical tubes.

steps.title: Virus Concentration
steps.instruction: Precipitate virions using NaCl and PEG 8000.

substeps.instruction: Weigh out 0.9 g sodium chloride (NaCl; Fisher Scientific™ BP358-10) and 4.0 g PEG 8000 (Fisher Scientific™ BP233-1) using an analytical balance and add to each sample tube.
Mix by inversion until the PEG/NaCl solids have dissolved and the mixture is translucent.
Store the samples overnight in a refrigerator at 4°C.

steps.title: RT-qPCR Data Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze amplification plots and calculate copies/L using the StepOnePlus TM software.

substeps.instruction: View the amplification plot and modify as needed using default baseline and threshold values.
View Ct values for each well and replicate group in the well or results table.
Generate slope, amplification efficiency, and R^2 values from the standard curve, adhering to MIQE standards.
Compare the current standard curve with a pooled average standard curve.
Re-run samples if amplification efficiency is not between 90-110%, R^2 is less than 0.97, or the slope differs by more than 10% compared to the pooled average curve.
